docs.title: What this repository is
docs.text:
This repository contains a GOV.UK Prototype Kit prototype for an Opal RM case creation journey.

It is a prototype, not a production service. That means:

  • speed and clarity matter more than heavy engineering patterns
  • there is no persistent backend or database
  • data is stored in the session only

docs.title: Useful local commands
docs.text:
Install dependencies:

npm install

Run the prototype locally:

npm run dev

Open the prototype:

http://localhost:3000

docs.title: Purpose and scope
docs.text:
This specification describes the prototype journey for adding an enforcement action to a respondent account. It currently supports one enforcement action type: Enforcement Summons (MSUMM).

The journey begins on the Enforcement tab. The at-a-glance Enforcement status panel communicates the account status but does not provide the add-action link.

This is a prototype specification. The action and its audit history are held in session data for the duration of the prototype session; they are not persisted to a backend service.

docs.title: Design-system references
docs.text:
• GOV.UK select
  • GOV.UK textarea
  • GOV.UK text input
  • GOV.UK error message and validation
  • GOV.UK summary list and summary card
  • GOV.UK inset text
  • MOJ date picker
  • MOJ autocomplete
  • MOJ alert

The source design is the Add enforcement action journey in Figma.

docs.title: Journey overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  A[Respondent account: Enforcement tab] --> B{Current enforcement action?}
  B -->|No| C[Add enforcement action]
  B -->|Yes| D[Cannot add enforcement action]
  C --> E{MSUMM selected?}
  E -->|No| C
  E -->|Yes| F[Enforcement Summons (MSUMM) details]
  F --> G{Valid fields?}
  G -->|No| F
  G -->|Yes| H[Check enforcement details]
  H -->|Change| F
  H -->|Submit| I[Create action with Scheduled hearing]
  I --> J[Enforcement tab with success message]

docs.title: Entry rules
docs.text:
• The journey is available from the Actions panel on the Enforcement tab.
  • The action link is labelled Add enforcement action.
  • The journey is for respondent accounts only.
  • Only one current enforcement action can exist on an account in the prototype.
  • If a current enforcement action exists, the user is shown the cannot-add screen instead of a new action form.
  • Direct navigation to an unknown account returns the user to the approved cases list.

docs.title: Page 1: Select an enforcement action
docs.text:
Route: GET /active-case/:id/enforcement/add Page title and H1: Add enforcement action

Screenshot placeholder: Add enforcement action — select action type.

The user selects an enforcement action and chooses Continue. The only available option is Enforcement Summons (MSUMM).

Field Component and rules Accessible name / ARIA Field-specific error message Enforcement action type GOV.UK select. Blank by default. The only available action is Enforcement Summons (MSUMM) with value msumm. Required. Visible label is programmatically associated with the select. Native select semantics are used; no additional ARIA is required. Select an enforcement action

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
• Continue: saves the draft selection and opens the MSUMM details page.
  • Cancel: returns to the Enforcement tab.
  • There is no back link on this page.

docs.title: Page 2: Enforcement Summons (MSUMM) details
docs.text:
Route: GET /active-case/:id/enforcement/msumm Page title and H1: Enforcement Summons (MSUMM)

Screenshot placeholder: Enforcement Summons (MSUMM) — hearing details and past-date warning.

The account number and respondent name are shown as a caption. The page has a Back link to the action-type selection page.

Field Component and rules Accessible name / ARIA Field-specific error message Reason GOV.UK textarea. Optional. Maximum 1,000 characters. Visible label is associated with the textarea. Reason must be 1,000 characters or fewer Court MOJ autocomplete populated from the England and Wales family court list. Required. Display width is two-thirds. Visible label is associated with the autocomplete input. The autocomplete provides its standard combobox semantics and keyboard behaviour. Select a court Hearing venue GOV.UK text input. Optional. Display width is two-thirds. Visible label is associated with the input. None. Hearing date MOJ date picker. Required. Accepts a real date in DD/MM/YYYY format. Dates in the past and future can be selected or entered. Visible label is associated with the date input. The past-date warning is a polite live region (role="status", aria-live="polite"). Enter hearing date; Enter a real hearing date in the format DD/MM/YYYY Hearing time GOV.UK text input. Optional. Must use 24-hour HH:MM format if entered; 00:00 represents midnight. Visible label and hint are associated with the input. Enter a hearing time in the format HH:MM

docs.title: Hearing date warning
docs.text:
When a valid hearing date earlier than today is entered or selected, show the warning immediately below the date picker:

Hearing date in the past You can continue with this date or change it

The warning:

  • uses the GOV.UK inset text component with the approved custom visual treatment: MOJ orange left border and light grey background
  • is hidden when the date is today, future, blank or invalid
  • does not prevent the user continuing
  • is announced politely to screen-reader users when it appears

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
• Back: returns to the action-type selection page.
  • Continue: validates the form, saves all entered values in the draft, and opens Check enforcement details.
  • Cancel: returns to the Enforcement tab and does not create an action.

docs.title: Page 3: Check enforcement details
docs.text:
Route: GET /active-case/:id/enforcement/check Page title and H1: Check enforcement details

Screenshot placeholder: Check enforcement details — Enforcement action summary card.

The page displays an Enforcement action summary card containing:

  • Enforcement action: Enforcement Summons (MSUMM), shown as a blue tag
  • Reason
  • Hearing court
  • Hearing venue
  • Hearing date in long date format
  • Hearing time

The card has a Change link that returns to the populated MSUMM details page. The link must not be blocked by a leave-page warning because the check page contains no editable, unsaved data.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
• Change: returns to the MSUMM details form with the draft values preserved.
  • Submit: creates the enforcement action.
  • Cancel: returns to the Enforcement tab and does not create an action.

docs.title: On submission
docs.text:
On successful submission:

  1. Create the enforcement action with:
  2. type: Enforcement Summons (MSUMM)
  3. hearing status: Scheduled
  4. the reason, court, venue, hearing date and hearing time entered by the user
  5. Add an Enforcement actions item to account history. It includes the MSUMM type, hearing date, court and, where supplied, the reason.
  6. Clear the enforcement-action draft.
  7. Redirect to the Enforcement tab.
  8. Show a dismissible MOJ success alert: Enforcement action added.

Screenshot placeholder: Enforcement tab after successful creation, with success alert and action summary card.

docs.title: Enforcement tab after creation
docs.text:
The Enforcement tab shows a summary card headed Last enforcement action. Its action is labelled Manage hearings; the future Manage hearings journey will define its destination and behaviour.

The card displays:

  • Enforcement action tag
  • Reason
  • Hearing status tag
  • Hearing court
  • Hearing venue
  • Hearing date
  • Hearing time

Hearing status tags are:

Status Tag treatment Scheduled Grey GOV.UK tag Result pending Yellow GOV.UK tag Resulted Default light-blue GOV.UK tag

docs.title: Active court-case banner
docs.text:
Show the account-level MOJ information alert directly below any success alert, and above the account header, whenever any enforcement action or application hearing has a status of Scheduled or Result pending.

The alert text is:

Account has one or more active court cases.

The banner is visible across the account tabs. It is not shown when every hearing is Resulted or when there are no active hearings.

docs.title: Cannot-add enforcement action
docs.text:
Route: GET /active-case/:id/enforcement/add when a current action exists

Screenshot placeholder: Cannot add enforcement action.

Show this message:

You cannot add an enforcement action while another enforcement action is active.

Provide a Back link to the Enforcement tab. Do not create or overwrite an action.

docs.title: Page-specific error messages
docs.text:
Page Condition Error summary and inline error Select an enforcement action No action selected Select an enforcement action MSUMM details Court is blank or not in the court list Select a court MSUMM details Hearing date is blank Enter hearing date MSUMM details Hearing date is not a real date in DD/MM/YYYY format Enter a real hearing date in the format DD/MM/YYYY MSUMM details Hearing time is supplied but not in 24-hour HH:MM format Enter a hearing time in the format HH:MM MSUMM details Reason exceeds 1,000 characters Reason must be 1,000 characters or fewer

A past hearing date is a warning, not an error, and must not appear in the error summary.

docs.title: Git and GitHub basics
docs.text: This page covers the small set of commands most people need every day.

docs.title: The safest daily workflow
docs.text:
Start from the latest main:

git checkout main
git pull --ff-only origin main

Create your own branch:

git checkout -b docs/my-change

Check what changed:

git status
git diff

Stage files:

git add README.md docs/

Commit:

git commit -m "docs: improve onboarding guide"

Push the branch for the first time:

git push -u origin docs/my-change

Later pushes:

git push

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
See your current branch:

git branch --show-current

Download new branches from GitHub:

git fetch origin

Switch to an existing branch:

git checkout branch-name

Show recent commit history:

git log --oneline --decorate -10

Discard an uncommitted change in one file:

git restore path/to/file

docs.title: How to raise a pull request
docs.text:
1. Push your branch.
  2. Open GitHub in the browser.
  3. Click Compare & pull request.
  4. Add a clear title and summary.
  5. Create the pull request.

For branches created inside this repository, the docs workflow publishes:

  • a branch preview
  • a pull request preview

The pull request gets a comment with the preview link.

docs.title: GitHub Pages publishing
docs.text:
This repository has two separate delivery paths:

  1. Azure App Service deployment for the prototype application
  2. GitHub Pages deployment for documentation

They are intentionally separate.

docs.title: What gets published
docs.text:
The documentation workflow publishes to three stable URL patterns:

  • latest/ for the current main branch documentation
  • branches/<branch-name>/ for branch previews
  • pulls/pr-<number>/ for pull request previews

Examples:

  • https://hmcts.github.io/opal-rm-prototype/latest/
  • https://hmcts.github.io/opal-rm-prototype/branches/readme_update/
  • https://hmcts.github.io/opal-rm-prototype/pulls/pr-123/

docs.title: One-time GitHub setup
docs.text:
A maintainer must do this once:

  1. Open the repository in GitHub.
  2. Go to Settings -> Pages.
  3. Choose Deploy from a branch.
  4. Select the gh-pages branch.
  5. Select the / (root) folder.
  6. Save the setting.

docs.title: Local preview for maintainers
docs.text:
If you want to preview the docs site locally before pushing:

python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

Then open:

http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: Safety rule for pull requests
docs.text:
PR previews are only published when the PR branch lives inside this repository.

Fork pull requests are excluded on purpose so the publishing workflow does not grant write-capable deployment behavior to untrusted branches.

docs.title: Why this repository uses gh-pages
docs.text:
This repository uses a workflow that writes static files to the gh-pages branch.

That approach is intentional because it allows multiple versions of the documentation to coexist at the same time:

  • latest/
  • branches/<branch-name>/
  • pulls/pr-<number>/

That is what makes branch and PR preview URLs possible without waiting for a merge to main.

docs.title: MacBook setup from scratch
docs.text:
These instructions assume:

  • you are using a new or reset MacBook
  • you have not set up Git before
  • you want a simple, repeatable setup

docs.title: Before you install anything
docs.text:
Make sure you have:

  1. Access to GitHub.
  2. Access to the hmcts/opal-rm-prototype repository.
  3. Permission to install software.
  4. A normal working folder, for example ~/Projects.

Do not keep the repository in iCloud Drive.

docs.title: Xcode Command Line Tools
docs.text:
Open Terminal and run:

xcode-select --install

docs.title: Homebrew
docs.text:
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

If Homebrew prints extra commands to add it to your shell profile, run them before continuing.

Check Homebrew:

brew --version

docs.title: Git and Visual Studio Code
docs.text:
brew install git
brew install --cask visual-studio-code

Check Git:

git --version

docs.title: Node.js 24 with nvm
docs.text:
brew install nvm
mkdir -p ~/.nvm

Resolve the correct Homebrew path first. This works on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs:

NVM_PREFIX="$(brew --prefix nvm)"

Add this to ~/.zshrc:

export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
export NVM_PREFIX="$(brew --prefix nvm)"
[ -s "$NVM_PREFIX/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_PREFIX/nvm.sh"
[ -s "$NVM_PREFIX/etc/bash_completion.d/nvm" ] && \. "$NVM_PREFIX/etc/bash_completion.d/nvm"

Restart Terminal, then run:

nvm install 24
nvm use 24
node --version
npm --version

docs.title: Set your Git identity and safe defaults
docs.text:
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git config --global pull.ff only
git config --global core.autocrlf input
git config --global core.eol lf
git config --global user.name "Your Full Name"
git config --global user.email "your.name@justice.gov.uk"

docs.title: Set up SSH for GitHub
docs.text:
Create the key:

mkdir -p ~/.ssh
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your.name@justice.gov.uk" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_hmcts

Create the HMCTS SSH alias:

cat <<'EOF' > ~/.ssh/config
Host github.com-hmcts
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_hmcts
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  IdentitiesOnly yes
EOF

Copy the key:

pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_hmcts.pub

Add it in GitHub under Settings -> SSH and GPG keys.

Test access:

ssh -T git@github.com-hmcts

docs.title: Clone and run the repository
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/Projects
cd ~/Projects
git clone git@github.com-hmcts:hmcts/opal-rm-prototype.git
cd opal-rm-prototype
npm install
npm run dev

Open:

http://localhost:3000

docs.title: First-time success checklist
docs.text:
You are ready if all of these are true:

  • git --version works
  • node --version works
  • npm --version works
  • ssh -T git@github.com-hmcts works
  • npm run dev starts the prototype

docs.title: REMO Active Account Usability Testing Script
Session Setup
docs.text:
Prototype URL: http://localhost:3050

Start each task from the Search page unless the participant is already on a relevant account page. Ask the participant to think aloud. Do not explain the navigation unless they are blocked and ask for help.

Use the sample data in this script only when the participant needs to enter new or changed information. The search criteria are chosen from records that exist in the prototype.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Thank you for taking part. We are testing the prototype, not you. Some things may not work as you expect, and that is useful for us to learn.

Please say what you are thinking as you work through each task. For example, what you are looking for, what you expect to happen, and anything that feels unclear.

docs.title: Resulting journeys — design specification
docs.text: Date: 21 October 2026 Status: Consolidated design specification for BA review Scope: Application and Enforcement hearing results; inputter and checker journeys

docs.title: 1. Purpose and authority
docs.text:
This document consolidates the eight BA Markdown write-ups supplied for Resulting and the subsequent decisions agreed with the designer. It describes the intended behaviour, rather than asserting that every rule is already implemented in the prototype.

Explicit decisions made during the review supersede conflicting wording in the supplied write-ups and older Figma frames. Existing checker behaviour is documented as a prototype baseline where it was not part of those decisions. Remaining dependencies and implementation gaps are listed at the end.

This is a GOV.UK Prototype Kit prototype. Use session data for draft and proposed changes. This specification does not require a database or production integration. References to shared data describe the intended service behaviour; a prototype session cannot demonstrate sharing between independent users.

docs.title: Source material
docs.text:
• Resulting designs
  • Review Add, Change and Remove route map
  • Supplied BA files: Results (inputter view); Outstanding hearings; Hearing information; Hearing outcome; Existing order details; Add results; Result details; Check and submit for validation.
  • Result-code workbook linked from the supplied Result details write-up. Its contents have not been independently verified for this specification; do not infer a complete result-code catalogue from the current prototype.

docs.title: Design-system references
docs.text:
• GOV.UK buttons, back links and tabs
  • GOV.UK tables and summary lists/cards
  • GOV.UK text inputs, character count, radios and checkboxes
  • GOV.UK error summaries, error messages and check answers
  • GOV.UK Prototype Components
  • MOJ date picker, sortable table, pagination, alert and timeline

Use established Nunjucks macros and design-system utilities. Do not introduce custom CSS or custom interaction patterns to match a frame.

docs.title: Roles, states and permissions
docs.text:
State Inputter behaviour Checker behaviour Account effect Result pending Record the hearing result. Not yet a submitted result to validate. Draft changes are not applied. Validation pending View the submitted result read-only. Review, validate or reject. Proposed order changes, remission and new hearings remain unapplied. Result rejected View review history, correct the draft and resubmit. View the rejected submission/history. Rejected proposals are not applied. Validated Excluded from outstanding and pending queues. No 24-hour Validated tab. Validation is recorded in history. Apply the validated proposals.

Judiciary and Legal adviser are an exception to deferred account changes: confirmed shared personnel updates affect all hearings at the same court on the same date, including already validated hearings. Do not describe these shared metadata updates as waiting for result validation.

docs.title: Display and accessibility
docs.text:
• Keep primary navigation on Resulting, Outstanding hearings, All rejected results and Validate results worklists.
  • Account links show the linked account number, then LASTNAME, Firstname underneath on lists and review screens. Hearing information uses the contextual display name, for example Mr Piotr NOWAK.
  • Format monetary summaries as £500.00 and £1,000.00. Retain payment frequency where relevant, for example £500.00 monthly.
  • Table dates use DD MMM YYYY, for example 01 Oct 2026. Date entry uses DD/MM/YYYY. Hearing-context summaries use day, full month and year.
  • Where a summary field has no data, show an em dash with an accessible name of No data, for example <span aria-label="No data">—</span>.
  • Use actual names in attendance questions, not placeholder tokens or “Defendant”.
  • Paginate lists with more than 25 rows using MOJ pagination. Preserve filters and sorting across pages.
  • Use native labels and component semantics. Add visually hidden context to repeated links rather than replacing visible labels with unrelated ARIA labels.
  • Errors appear in a GOV.UK error summary and beside the field. Summary links target the relevant field. Preserve submitted values and use standard focus behaviour.
  • Removal success messages use MOJ alert with variant: "success" and dismissible: true. Store before redirecting, consume on the destination and do not repeat on refresh.

docs.title: 3. Journey sequence
docs.text:
1. Open Outstanding hearings from Resulting or Cases, or start Record result from the account's relevant hearing.
  2. Select a Result pending hearing and complete Hearing information.
  3. For an Application, choose Hearing outcome. Enforcement bypasses this screen.
  4. On the Application order route, review existing orders and optionally add/amend terms.
  5. Record results through the initial Add results journey. At least one result is required except on the Application order route with at least one term.
  6. Check and submit for validation. Add, change or remove results from review as needed.
  7. Submit and return to Outstanding hearings with the court/date filters retained.
  8. The checker validates or rejects the submission.
  9. A rejected result can be corrected by an inputter and resubmitted.

docs.title: Result requirement matrix
docs.text:
Hearing and route Can review show No results? Can submit with No results? Application: Add or amend order terms, with at least one term Yes Yes Application: No order terms to add or amend Yes, including after removing the final result No Enforcement Yes, including after removing the final result No

Do not force a user away from review simply because they removed the last result. Enforce the submission requirement when they attempt to submit.

docs.title: 15. Cancellation and return context
docs.text:
Remember the journey's original entry point separately from any local review-edit return point.

Context Confirmed Cancel Decline cancellation Recording started from Outstanding hearings Discard the unsaved hearing-result draft and proposed order changes. Return to Outstanding hearings with court/date filters retained. Stay on the current page with entries intact. Recording started from account details Discard the unsaved hearing-result draft and proposed order changes. Return to the originating account details screen. Preserve the originating tab where available. Stay on the current page. Local edit/add opened from review Discard only the current unsaved local operation. Preserve the rest of the draft and return to the original review. Stay on the edit form. Checker Cancel Leave without recording a decision and return to the checker worklist. No proposed result changes are applied.

Cancel accessible text identifies the real destination, for example Cancel and return to review, rather than always saying Outstanding hearings. Use the existing leave-confirmation pattern. Confirmed result removal is separate from cancelling an unsaved edit.

docs.title: Validation and rejection effects
docs.text:
• Validate: apply proposed order changes and remission; create every proposed Application hearing; record validation in history; remove the submission from the pending queue. Return to Validate results with Hearing result validated. Account changes have been applied.
  • Reject: retain the proposal for correction, set Result rejected and add the reason to Review history. Do not apply proposed changes. Return to Validate results with Hearing result rejected and returned to the inputter.

Add results and Change return to the rejected review that opened them, not the new-result Check and submit page. Results can be removed through confirmation; an empty review remains accessible, subject to the submission matrix. Proposed order changes remain unapplied until validation.

Submit for validation returns the result to Validation pending and retains the review history. Use the same submission destination and retained court/date context as the recording journey. Preservation of the all-rejected origin for Back navigation is separate from submission destination.

docs.title: 19. Acceptance checks
docs.text:
1. Resulting has only Validation pending and Rejected; Action sorts; All rejected results includes other users' submissions.
  2. Outstanding hearings retains primary navigation, filters independently by court/date, paginates at 25, and defaults to date/court/respondent surname ascending.
  3. Status determines action consistently: Record result for Result pending; View result for pending validation/rejected.
  4. Judiciary is required and limited to 250; Legal adviser is optional with the magistrates hint. Enforcement alone displays remission.
  5. Shared edits require confirmation, including when opened from review, and affect already validated hearings at the same court/date.
  6. Remission accepts 500/500.00/500.50, rejects 500.5, zero and amounts above total account arrears.
  7. Existing terms can continue unchanged. Application order route has at least one term but may have no manually added results.
  8. Duplicate result codes remain distinct. Change edits only the selected entry; Remove removes only that entry.
  9. Review Add results opens the standalone blank selector; Change opens prefilled details directly; successful saves return to the invoking review.
  10. Removing the last result on review stays on review, shows No results/Add results and a dismissible one-time Result removed alert. Mandatory-result submission remains blocked.
  11. A new result's court is blank; an existing result's court is retained when edited. Time accepts only valid 24-hour HH:MM and uses a compact input.
  12. Multiple new hearings are all created under Applications on validation; no first-result-only truncation occurs.
  13. Cancel returns to the original journey entry and discards the draft; local review Cancel discards only the local edit. A confirmed shared update is not rolled back.
  14. Submission returns to filtered Outstanding hearings; inputter pending is read-only. Validation applies proposals; rejection does not; history remains visible.
  15. Missing data, link context, keyboard behaviour, error focus, conditional controls, pagination and screen-reader sorting announcements receive manual checks.

docs.title: 20. Dependencies, design tidy-up and prototype differences
docs.text:
These items must remain visible when handing this specification to delivery teams. They are not evidence that the corresponding behaviour has already been implemented.

Item Status / required work Result-code workbook Required to complete per-code fields, options, validation, bounds and hearing-creation mapping. Current prototype has a simplified Reason/MADJ form, not the full configurable catalogue. Outstanding hearings naming and tie-break sorting Agreed target; reconcile prototype headings, navigation and date/court/surname ordering. Shared details confirmation from review Agreed target; the reviewed prototype bypassed confirmation for review-entry edits. Also update confirmation text to state that validated hearings are included. Remission amount bounds Agreed target; existing prototype decimal syntax alone does not enforce positive value and total-arrears maximum. Multiple created Application hearings Agreed target; reviewed submission/validation code retained only one proposed hearing and needs extension. docs.title: Search flows and logic
docs.text: This page documents the Search journey in the prototype for functional specification work. It covers the user flows, search criteria, matching rules, result handling, and prototype-specific notes for simple search and advanced search.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
The Search journey lets a user find cases and accounts, then open the relevant respondent, applicant, minor creditor, or major creditor account.

Search is available from /search and is shown as the active Search item in the service navigation.

The current prototype uses in-memory prototype data. It does not call a backend, database, or external search service.

docs.title: Screen Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  A["Search page"] --> B["User enters simple search criteria"]
  A --> C["User opens advanced search and enters advanced criteria"]
  B --> D["Submit search"]
  C --> D
  D --> E{"Simple and advanced criteria both entered?"}
  E -->|Yes| F["Conflicting criteria screen"]
  E -->|No| G{"No searchable criteria entered?"}
  G -->|Yes| A
  G -->|No| H{"Major creditor only?"}
  H -->|Yes| I{"Major creditor account found?"}
  I -->|Yes| J["Major creditor account page"]
  I -->|No| K["No results screen"]
  H -->|No| L["Run case and account search"]
  L --> M{"Number of matches"}
  M -->|0| K
  M -->|More than 100| N["Too many results screen"]
  M -->|1 to 100| O["Search results page"]
  O --> P["Open respondent, applicant, or minor creditor account"]

docs.title: Search Page
docs.text:
The main search page is titled "Search for cases and accounts".

Simple search is shown first. Advanced search is hidden in a GOV.UK details component labelled "or use advanced search". Advanced search uses tabs for:

  • Respondents
  • Applicants
  • Minor creditors
  • Major creditors

There is also an "Active accounts only" checkbox in the advanced search section. It is checked by default in the interface.

docs.title: Visible criteria
docs.text:
The visible simple search field is:

Field Purpose Account number Find a case by respondent, applicant, minor creditor, or major creditor account number.

docs.title: Supported server-side criteria
docs.text:
The route also supports a reference-number field, although that field is not currently visible on the search page template. The conflict screen describes this as "a reference or case number".

If the reference number field is posted, it searches against:

  • REMO reference
  • case reference

docs.title: Simple search matching rules
docs.text:
Account number search:

  • must match an account number exactly after normalising spaces and hyphens
  • checks respondent account numbers, applicant account numbers, minor creditor account numbers, and major creditor account numbers
  • uses account prefixes generated by the prototype:
  • RP for respondent accounts
  • AP for applicant accounts
  • MC for minor creditor accounts
  • MA for major creditor accounts

Reference number search:

  • matches against the REMO reference or case reference
  • is case-insensitive
  • ignores spaces and hyphens
  • supports partial matching

docs.title: Advanced Search
docs.text: Advanced search lets the user search using respondent, applicant, minor creditor, or major creditor details.

docs.title: Respondent fields
docs.text: Field Matching rule Last name Case-insensitive partial match First names Case-insensitive partial match Date of birth Exact date match after normalisation Postal or zip code Partial compact match, ignoring spaces and hyphens

docs.title: Applicant fields
docs.text: Field Matching rule Last name Case-insensitive partial match First names Case-insensitive partial match Date of birth Exact date match after normalisation Postal or zip code Partial compact match, ignoring spaces and hyphens

docs.title: Minor creditor fields
docs.text:
The minor creditor tab has a radio choice for "Individual" or "Company".

Individual fields:

Field Matching rule Last name Case-insensitive partial match First names Case-insensitive partial match Postal or zip code Partial compact match, ignoring spaces and hyphens

Company fields:

Field Matching rule Company name Case-insensitive partial match Postal or zip code Partial compact match, ignoring spaces and hyphens

For a minor creditor search, the case must have at least one minor creditor that matches all the minor creditor criteria entered.

docs.title: Major creditor field
docs.text:
The major creditor tab uses an autocomplete control with central authority options, for example "Central Authority - Australia".

If a major creditor is the only advanced search criterion:

  • the prototype looks for a major creditor account with that major creditor code
  • if found, the user is taken directly to the major creditor account page
  • if not found, the user is taken to the no results screen

If a major creditor is combined with other advanced search criteria:

  • it acts as another filter
  • the case must match the other advanced criteria and have a major creditor account with the selected major creditor code

docs.title: Combining Criteria
docs.text:
The user must search using either simple search criteria or advanced search criteria, not both.

If the user enters both:

  • an account number or reference number, and
  • any respondent, applicant, minor creditor, or major creditor field

they are shown the conflicting criteria screen.

Within advanced search, criteria are combined using "and" logic:

  • if respondent fields are entered, all entered respondent fields must match
  • if applicant fields are entered, all entered applicant fields must match
  • if minor creditor fields are entered, one minor creditor on the case must match all entered minor creditor fields
  • if a major creditor is selected with other criteria, the case must also have that major creditor
  • if "Active accounts only" is selected, the case status must be Active

The active accounts checkbox does not count as a searchable criterion on its own. If it is the only selected option and no search fields are entered, the user is returned to the search page.

docs.title: Normalisation Rules
docs.text:
Before matching, the prototype normalises some values:

Value type Normalisation General text Trimmed and converted to lowercase Compact text, such as account numbers and postcodes Trimmed, lowercased, and spaces and hyphens removed Dates Normalised to DD/MM/YYYY where possible

Accepted date formats include:

  • YYYY-MM-DD
  • D/M/YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY
  • written dates such as 15 March 1975

Dates must match exactly after normalisation.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
If the search returns no matches, the user is shown the no results screen.

If the search returns more than 100 matches, the user is shown the too many results screen and asked to narrow the search.

If the search returns between 1 and 100 matches:

  • the matching rows are stored in session data
  • the user is redirected to the search results page
  • the results table shows:
  • respondent account
  • applicant account
  • minor creditor accounts
  • status
  • arrears
  • respondent, applicant, and minor creditor account numbers are links to their account pages
  • if there are more than 25 results, MOJ pagination is shown
  • each results page shows 25 results

docs.title: Error And Exception Screens
docs.text: Scenario Destination User-facing message Simple and advanced criteria are both entered /search/conflicting-criteria "You cannot search using a quick search field and advanced search fields at the same time" No matching results /search/no-results "There are no matching results." More than 100 matching results /search/too-many-results "There are more than 100 results. Narrow your search to see fewer results." No criteria entered /search The user is returned to the search page.

docs.title: Prototype Data Notes
docs.text:
Search runs against the compact searchData list in app/routes.js. That data is also used to populate respondent and creditor account records for the account pages.

The current prototype data includes:

  • respondent accounts
  • applicant accounts
  • minor creditor accounts
  • one major creditor account for Central Authority - Australia

The minor creditor company search path exists in the route logic, but the current compact search data contains individual minor creditor records rather than company minor creditor records. Unless company minor creditor data is added, company searches are likely to return no results.

The route reads address line 1 fields for respondent, applicant, and minor creditor searches, but those address line 1 fields are not currently displayed on the search page. The visible address-related fields are postal or zip code fields.

docs.text:

  • Search exception templates: app/views/search/conflicting-criteria.html, app/views/search/no-results.html, app/views/search/too-many-results.html
  • Search route and matching logic: app/routes.js, search section from // -- Search
  • Major creditor autocomplete options: majorCreditorOptions in app/routes.js
  • Major creditor prototype account data: majorCreditorAccounts in app/routes.js

docs.title: Using Codex for prototyping
docs.text: This guide is for business analysts and designers who want to use Codex to help change the prototype.

docs.title: How to start Codex for this repository
docs.text:
Start Codex from the repository root so it can inspect the right files.

  1. Open Terminal on Mac or Git Bash on Windows.
  2. Move into the repository folder:
cd ~/Projects/opal-rm-prototype
  1. Check you are in the right folder:
pwd
git status
  1. If this is your first use on that machine, sign in:
codex login
  1. Start the interactive Codex session:
codex
  1. Paste one of the prompts from this guide.
  2. Review the files Codex changed with git status and git diff.
  3. Run the prototype with npm run dev and check the result in your browser.

If the terminal says codex is not recognised, stop there and ask your team how Codex is installed on your HMCTS laptop before going further.

docs.title: What Codex is good at in this repository
docs.text:
Codex is useful for:

  • adding a new page to the prototype journey
  • changing wording on existing pages
  • moving or adding journey steps
  • replacing custom markup with GOV.UK or MOJ components
  • improving page structure so it is easier to test with users
  • explaining which files control a screen or a journey

Codex is less useful if your request is vague.

Good:

  • "Add an interpreter needs page after hearing details."
  • "Change the review screen so it shows a warning when the email is missing."
  • "Use GOV.UK radios instead of a select on the case type page."

Weak:

  • "Improve this."
  • "Make it better."
  • "Do something modern."

docs.title: How this prototype is structured
docs.text:
These are the files Codex will usually need to change:

  • app/views/ for page templates
  • app/routes.js for navigation and flow logic
  • app/data/session-data-defaults.js for default answers or stored session values
  • app/filters.js for template filters
  • app/assets/javascripts/application.js for small front-end behaviour
  • app/assets/sass/application.scss for small style changes

docs.title: Rules Codex should follow here
docs.text:
This repository is a GOV.UK Prototype Kit prototype, so the safest instructions are:

  • use GOV.UK Design System and MOJ Design System components
  • prefer Nunjucks macros instead of hand-written HTML
  • keep styling changes small
  • keep the repository as a prototype, not a production application
  • do not add a backend, database, or API layer unless explicitly asked

docs.title: Add a page
docs.text: Add a new page to this prototype after the hearing details step. The page should ask whether an interpreter is required. Use GOV.UK radios, save the answer in session data, and update app/routes.js so the journey continues to the review page.

docs.title: Change page content
docs.text: Update the review page so the applicant and respondent details are easier to read. Use GOV.UK summary lists and clear headings.

docs.title: Ask for an explanation first
docs.text: Explain this prototype repository to me as a business analyst. Show me which files I would change for page content, flow logic, and styling.

docs.title: Make a page more GOV.UK-aligned
docs.text: Refactor this page to use GOV.UK or MOJ macros where possible. Keep the prototype simple and easy to change.

docs.title: Add a warning or condition
docs.text: If no respondent email has been entered, show a GOV.UK warning text on the review page and explain which file you changed.

docs.title: Best way to work with Codex
docs.text:
1. Say what page or journey step you want to change.
  2. Say what the user should see or be able to do.
  3. Say whether the answer should affect the next page.
  4. Ask Codex to explain which files it changed.

docs.title: A simple BA or designer workflow
docs.text:
1. Run the prototype locally with npm run dev.
  2. Open the current page in the browser.
  3. Write down what you want to change.
  4. Give Codex a precise instruction.
  5. Run the prototype again and check the result in the browser.
  6. If needed, ask Codex for a refinement.

docs.title: If you are not sure where to start
docs.text:
Use this:

I am a business analyst working on this GOV.UK prototype. Explain the journey structure and then make the smallest change needed to add a new question page before the review page.

If you want a safer first run, use this instead:

I am new to Codex and this repository. First explain which files control the page content, the flow logic, and the styling. Then make one very small prototype-safe change and tell me exactly which files changed.

docs.title: View and amend orders QA differences
docs.text: Compared against the RM write-ups in /Users/douglasmaitland/Downloads on 14 July 2026.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The prototype broadly contains the journeys described in the write-ups for the Orders tab, changing order details, adding and amending order terms, viewing previous terms, changing interest and indexation, and changing managing payments.

The main gaps are validation, route-guard behaviour, the "use this creditor for all order terms" option, and parts of the amend-order-term creditor journey.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: Area Write-up says Prototype behaviour Difference Orders tab: previous terms link "View previous terms" opens in a new window and ARIA text says it opens in a new window. The link opens in the same window. Creditor account links open in a new window. Mismatch with Orders tab.md and View previous order terms.md. Change order details: court and order date Court and date order made are mandatory. On active accounts, both labels include "(optional)" and validation allows them to be blank. Mismatch with Change order details.md. Change order details: future date errors Future dates should show "Date cannot be in the future". Validation text is "Future dates are invalid". Content mismatch. Change interest and indexation Interest and indexation selections are mandatory, with error messages if missing. Posting the form with no selections redirects back to the Orders tab and saves blanks. Missing validation and error summary. Change managing payments Payment arrangement is mandatory, with "Select payment arrangement" if missing. Posting the form with no selection redirects back to the Orders tab and saves a blank value. Missing validation and error summary. Add order terms: no selection Error should be "Select an order". Error is "Select an order term from the list." Content mismatch. Add/amend order term details validation Decimal, date format, two-decimal-place, child DOB, and character validation should be enforced. The dynamic field validation mainly checks required fields and text length. Dates and decimal formats are not fully validated against the write-up rules. Missing validation. Select creditor: major creditor If "Major creditor" is selected, selecting the major creditor name is mandatory. Selecting "Major creditor" with no name continues to the review page and labels the creditor as "Major creditor". Missing validation. Select creditor: apply to all Write-up includes "Use this creditor for all order terms". No checkbox is shown in the creditor screen or minor-creditor-added state. Missing feature. Amend order terms: add new minor creditor The select-creditor screen is shared by add and amend journeys, including "Add a new minor creditor". In the amend journey, selecting "Add new minor creditor" shows "Select a creditor" instead of starting the add-minor-creditor sub-journey. Amend path is incomplete. Add minor creditor validation Minor creditor type, names, address, and bank details have required and format errors. The add-minor-creditor route stores submitted values without validation. Missing validation. Cancel behaviour If the user has started entering information, cancel should show a route guard. Cancel links return to the Orders tab or clear the add-order-term state without a route guard. Missing route guard across these journeys. Review order terms changes Add journey button should be "Submit"; amend journey button should be "Save changes". Add journey uses "Add order terms"; amend journey uses "Save changes". Add journey button text mismatch.

docs.title: Windows setup from scratch
docs.text:
These instructions assume:

  • you are using an HMCTS-managed Windows laptop
  • you have not set up Git before
  • you want the safest path with the fewest surprises

docs.title: Before you install anything
docs.text:
Check that you have:

  1. Access to GitHub.
  2. Access to the hmcts/opal-rm-prototype repository.
  3. Permission to install software.
  4. A normal working folder, for example C:\Users\<your-name>\Projects.

Do not clone the repository into OneDrive or a shared network folder.

docs.title: Visual Studio Code
docs.text:
1. Go to https://code.visualstudio.com/.
  2. Download the Windows installer.
  3. Install it using default options.

docs.title: Git for Windows
docs.text:
1. Go to https://git-scm.com/download/win.
  2. Download and run the installer.
  3. Keep the default options unless your team tells you otherwise.
  4. Open Git Bash when the install finishes.

Check Git:

git --version

docs.title: Node.js 24
docs.text:
Recommended approach:

  1. Install nvm-windows from https://github.com/coreybutler/nvm-windows/releases.
  2. Open a new Git Bash window.

nvm install 24.0.0
nvm use 24.0.0

npm --version

docs.title: Set your Git identity and safe defaults
docs.text:
Open Git Bash and run:

git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git config --global pull.ff only
git config --global core.autocrlf input
git config --global core.eol lf
git config --global user.name "Your Full Name"

docs.text:
Create the key:

mkdir -p ~/.ssh
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your.name@justice.gov.uk" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_hmcts

Create the HMCTS SSH alias:

cat <<'EOF' > ~/.ssh/config
Host github.com-hmcts
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_hmcts
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  IdentitiesOnly yes
EOF

Copy the public key:

cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_hmcts.pub | clip

Then add it in GitHub under Settings -> SSH and GPG keys.

Test access:

ssh -T git@github.com-hmcts

mkdir -p ~/Projects
cd ~/Projects

cd opal-rm-prototype

npm run dev

http://localhost:3000
